messages:
ana: FYI our hardware partner uploaded a quarterly bulk usage bundle to S3 but the records are messy: missing entitlement_id on many rows and several retried slices have duplicated payloads with differing event_ids. We need a replay/playbook so we don't double-charge or lose credit.

sam: Are the files accompanied by a manifest or checksum so we can verify file integrity?

maria: They included a manifest.json with md5 per file but no per-record signatures. The duplicates are from their uploader doing slice retries and emitting new event_ids.

jordan: Plan suggestion: compute an idempotency key in ingest: sha256(partner_id|original_event_id|usage_window). Use that to dedupe on write. For records without original_event_id, fall back to hash(payload) but flag as low-confidence.

lee: Mapping entitlements by customer_email is risky (account merges/moves). Prefer explicit entitlement_id. If missing, try deterministic lookups: account_id -> entitlement at timestamp, billing_customer_id lookup, then email. If still ambiguous, mark for manual reconciliation and do not bill.

ana: Can we ask the partner to include original_event_timestamp and entitlement_id in future exports? That would make replay safe.

maria: They're willing to add those fields going forward, but not retroactively. So we need a robust ingest for current blobs.

sam: Drafted ingestion phases:
1) file validation: check manifest md5s, reject corrupted files
2) parse & normalize: standardize field names, note missing fields
3) dedupe & insert: compute idempotency key, upsert with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
4) enrichment: attempt entitlement resolution; if unresolved -> status="pending_entitlement" (non-billable) and create ticket

jordan: Pseudo-SQL for dedupe:
```
WITH rows AS (SELECT compute_key(partner_id, original_event_id, window) AS k, * FROM parsed)
INSERT INTO marketplace_usage (idempotency_key, partner_id, event_id, usage, entitlement_id, status)
SELECT k, partner_id, event_id, usage, entitlement_id, 'ingested' FROM rows
ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING;
```
Then update rows where entitlement_id is NULL -> status='pending_entitlement' and emit reconciliation signals.

lee: We need a retention & SLA policy for pending_entitlement. Recommend 45 days active window; after that auto-issue a credit and mark partner_reconciliation_needed. Capture audit trail for every auto-credit.

ana: Sounds good. We'll also need a replay report for the partner: counts for accepted, deduped/skipped, pending, rejected (checksum fail), with S3 path and manifest hash.

maria: I'll draft the CSV report format. Include: record_id, action(ingested|skipped|pending|rejected), reason, entitlement_resolution_hint, trace_id.

sam: Ops runbook notes:
- who triggers replay: @jordan
- run dry-run mode first to see counts (no writes)
- limit replay to events <= 90 days old for now
- require a manual sign-off before creating credits

jordan: I'll build a replay CLI: `redwood-replay --partner hwco --s3 s3://hwco/dumps/q1.tar.gz --dry-run` which emits a CSV of planned actions. After review, re-run without --dry-run to apply. Deploy behind feature flag.

ops-bot: deployment queued: infra/replay-worker v1.4 -> staging.

lee: After staging checks, run a canary: process 5% of the bundle and compare billing delta chart for anomalies.

ana: I'll own partner comms: send timeline, ask for schema additions (original_event_timestamp, entitlement_id), and promise replay report. @maria will review before send.

maria: Reviewing now; adding a template and sample rows to the report.

sam: Summary of action items:
- jordan: implement CLI, idempotency + dry-run (ETA 48h)
- maria: partner message + report template (ETA EOD)
- lee: reconciliation job + auto-credit policy docs (ETA 4 days)
- ana: coordinate partner schema onboarding (ETA next week)

ana: Treat as P1 for billing integrity. We'll meet again after first dry-run. :white_check_mark:
